result.answer: Plan A costs $120 per month, supports 40 concurrent requests, and performs recovery checkpoints every 10 seconds. Plan B costs $75 per month, supports 24 concurrent requests, and performs checkpoints every 30 seconds. Evidence from the stress test ledger indicates that while both plans performed within capacity up to 24 active requests (Trial 16), Plan B saturated at its declared limit in Trial 17 (25 active requests), failing to process additional load beyond 960 completed requests in all subsequent trials. In contrast, Plan A continued to scale linearly with load, handling up to 44 active requests (Trial 36) without saturation. Although Plan B offers a lower monthly cost, it incurs higher latency (e.g., p95 657 ms vs 504 ms at 40 requests in Trial 32) and risks data loss due to less frequent checkpoints. The tradeoff confirms that lower monthly cost alone does not establish superior user response latency or system stability under load.

sections.text: Plan A is priced at $120 per month with a 10-second recovery checkpoint interval and a capacity of 40 concurrent requests. Plan B is priced at $75 per month with a 30-second recovery checkpoint interval and a capacity of 24 concurrent requests.

The stress test ledger shows that Plan B saturated above its declared capacity starting at Trial 17 with 25 active requests, maintaining a flat completion count of 960 requests thereafter. Plan A successfully handled increasing loads up to its limit, completing 1600 requests at 40 active requests in Trial 32.

The primary tradeoff is between cost and performance reliability. Plan B saves $45 monthly but suffers from capacity saturation and higher latency under load. As noted in the product trial conclusion, lower monthly cost alone does not establish superior user response latency.
